verdict.rationale: GrowthBook documents a REST API it calls "full", with specific endpoints for toggling features and pulling experiment results, and its MCP server works by calling that API. A runtime probe also created a user, organization, feature, and SDK connection through the API. However, nothing shows that every UI capability (visual editor, fact tables/metrics, approvals, dashboards) is reachable through the API. The 'require confirmation' guardrail means some risky changes still need a person to confirm them in GrowthBook. missing for 10: documented endpoint-by-endpoint parity with the UI, API coverage of the visual editor, metrics/fact tables and approval flows, a published OpenAPI spec (probe paths returned 404), independent corroboration of parity

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: GrowthBook offers a full REST API for interacting with the application.
automate it (for example, from a deploy script) with the toggle feature endpoint, which switches a flag on or off in one or more environments.
Get results for an experiment (`GET /v1/experiments/{id}/results`) to pull the latest analysis into your own reporting.
the first user and organization were created through the API, a boolean feature `pa-probe-flag` was created, an SDK connection was minted
makes authenticated calls to the GrowthBook REST API
